holidays.name: National Sunglasses Day
holidays.description: Put on your shades and strike a pose. This sunny day celebrates the accessory that makes everyone look a little cooler while protecting their eyes from the summer glare.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance, widely listed in the United States and Canada. It is timed for the height of summer, when sunglasses are at their most useful.
holidays.funFact: Sunglasses date back to 12th-century China, where judges wore smoked-quartz lenses to hide their expressions in court. The lenses had no sun-protection purpose.

holidays.name: National Ice Cream Cake Day
holidays.description: A day for layered, frosty, fork-required bliss. Ice cream cake combines two beloved desserts, so it is one of the most delicious ways to beat the summer heat.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It lands in the middle of ice cream season, which suits it well.
holidays.funFact: Ice cream cakes became a freezer-aisle staple in the 20th century, and Carvel's Fudgie the Whale and Cookie Puss cakes became cult favorites.

holidays.name: Helen Keller Day
holidays.description: A day honoring Helen Keller, the author, lecturer, and activist who became a global symbol of determination. It celebrates her life and her advocacy for people with disabilities.
holidays.origin: It marks her birthday, June 27, 1880, in Tuscumbia, Alabama. In the United States it was recognized by a presidential proclamation on the 100th anniversary of her birth.
holidays.funFact: Keller became the first deafblind person to earn a Bachelor of Arts degree, graduating from Radcliffe College in 1904.
